1.sofaString: 367	Pt, ******, is a 14 year old male, diagnosed with a complex history of congenital heart disease including dextrocardia, tricuspid atresia, hypoplastic RV, restrictive VSD, and L-TGA. He is s/p atrial septectomy (2003), s/p bidirectional ***** (2004), s/p VSD enlargement (2005) and s/p fenestrated ****** (2007). He ultimately required pacemaker placement (2017). He now presents with failing ****** physiology with more frequent PLE exacerbations. He was transferred to our facility for transplant evaluation. He was referred by ***** ******  **** for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt, his parents, and review of the medical records.   SW spent 90 minutes of face to face time with patient's family.     Living situation:  **, ******, resides with his mother in *** **** ******, **.  They reside in a single family house with central air conditioning and city water. They use bottled water for drinking.  They change the air filter every 3 months.  There is no smoking in the home.    They have an indoor cat, but ****** does not go near the ****** box.  ****** sees his dad but does not go to his dad's home, as dad has a roommate residing there as well.  Dad resides in ****** *******, **.       Demographics:  Mother: ***** *******  DOB:  **/**/****   Age:  43  Born in ****  Employment:  None currently  Education: Just completed RN program at ********* ******* in ****. She has not yet taken test for licensure however due to pt's medical issues since then.   Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)  Email: ************@*******.***     Father: ****** *******  DOB:  **/**/****   Age: 41  Employment:  Works for *****  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Siblings:  None     Support systems:  Parents divorced in 2010.  Mom has primary custody and states she does the primary medical decision making. She states dad is in agreement with this.  Mom states that her mother and brothers reside nearby in *** **** ******. She states they provide additional support to her and ******.       Both parents have a car, and state travel to Gainesville is not problematic. However, both parents state the cost of the gas may become problematic.       Mom states she is a ********* and would like to have a chaplain involved during ******'s admissions.  She is not opposed to blood products/ transfusions.       ****** is a personable, intelligent teenager who presents emotionally younger than his stated age.  He is in the 9th grade.  He did a combination of attending ****** *** doing part-time homebound instruction last year. This is the first year that he is doing fulltime homebound instruction.  He states it does not bother him that he is no longer attending school.  ****** is reportedly in gifted program, and is currently enrolled in ****** and AP classes.  He hopes to eventually become a cardiologist.         ****** enjoys *****.  He also enjoys classical music.  He is interested in trying the VR machine that Child **** has.  ****** states he likes to research things and learn. He disclosed he has researched his medical condition and his medications. He does not like to be started on new meds without being advised of interaction and side effects with other medications, and the impact on his overall health. He states he likes to know the purpose of each medication and how it works in his body.  He is ********* compliant with his meds, and is independent in taking them[SM1].       ****** is also interested in nutrition. He does not like to eat 'junk food' and prefers to eat foods that will improve his health.  He is aware of the PLE and need for certain nutrition.    Mom states that he was recently started on pediasure peptide as the protein in this is more broken down and easier for him to digest.  However, she states the insurance will not cover this as it is indicated for children under the age of 13.  SW advised that *** *** ** or MD to write a prior auth indicating the rationale for why it is indicated for ******, despite his age being above the age limits.     Course of illness:         ******, is a 14 year old male, diagnosed with a complex history of congenital heart disease including dextrocardia, tricuspid atresia, hypoplastic RV, restrictive VSD, and L-TGA. He is s/p atrial septectomy (2003), s/p bidirectional ***** (2004), s/p VSD enlargement (2005) and s/p fenestrated ****** (2007). He ultimately required pacemaker placement (2017). He now presents with failing ****** physiology with more frequent PLE exacerbations. He was transferred to our facility for transplant evaluation.  However, mom is in communication with a hospital in ********.  She states they will be having a conference within the next week, with plans to schedule ****** to go there sometime in ********* for ****************. Both she and ****** express belief that this procedure will 'fix' his symptoms and allow him to avoid transplant.  They are open to transplant evaluation, but do not believe he needs transplant at this time.      Financial Situation:     ****** is covered by Medicaid ********/ ********.  The family is supported by child support from dad and by ******'s SSI income.  Mom reports no other income.  She states she is not losing income while being at bedside with ******. However, she states it does become more financially stressful due to added expenses for food, travel, etc.  She disclosed she had hoped to be working as an RN by the time he needed transplant so that she would have higher income and better insurance coverage.      ****** seems to be very aware of the family's financial status, and appeared anxious when mom got a hotel room for the night in order to get some rest. ****** disclosed to SW that it cost $100 for that one night. He states that they cannot afford that.     Dad is employed at ***** and pays child support to the family.  Dad states he tries to help out additionally when possible, but does not have a lot of room in his budget either.  He admits that the displacement expenses secondary to our program being in Gainesville will be a challenge for him as well. He states this will limit his ability to be present, as he will need to continue working as much as possible.     Information on fundraising through **** was provided.  The First Hand Foundation ***** was also discussed.  Parents are interested in pursuing both.     Family History:     Mom denies any other cardiac history in the family, other than ******. She states her mother has diabetes and hypertension.  She states that she and dad are both healthy.     Mom states she has a history of anxiety and depression. She has been on psychotropic meds in the past but is not currently.  She states ****** has episodes on depression and anxiety, but has never been diagnosed with any mental health disorder. He is opposed to being on any psychotropic meds.  He reportedly also has had panic attacks. He states he is able to get through these on his own, after several minutes.  Mom states ****** appears to have PTSD when any hospital show comes on the TV.         There is no reported family history of substance abuse issues. There was one incident of DV between parents about 7 years ago.  The parents are now divorced, and have a good relationship with one another. They are able to get along well.  Dad has been here this admission, and has been driving mom to and from hotel, Target, etc. He plans to transport mom and ****** home upon discharge as mom **** in ambulance and does not have her car here.  There is no other reported legal history or involvement with DCF.         Adherence:  There are no reported concerns for adherence identified.  ****** reportedly is very independent in taking his meds.  Mom monitors but does not have concerns regarding his compliance.  The family has no documented history of missing appointments.  ****** states he is able to do labs and needle ***** without difficulty. He states he is used to it by now.  He also is compliant with diet and exercise.         Assessment and recommendations:     ****** initially was resistant to the idea of transplant, and expressed hope that the procedure in ******** (lymphangioplasty) would 'fix' everything so he would not require transplant.  Parents express some hope that this will help, but understand that transplant may be his only option.  Parents are in agreement with moving forward with listing for transplant, in case he does require it. Mom verbalized hesitation regarding listing initially. However, she states that she had thought he would not be able to be listed at another center. Now that she knows he can be listed at multiple sites, she is in agreement with moving forward.  Dad verbalizes feeling that there are only 2 options:  pursue the procedure in ******** or pursue transplant.  He states it has been financially challenging to be here in Gainesville just for this brief admission. He states they will need to plan for transplant as it would be much ********* admission/ displacement period.  He describes feeling better knowing the resources that would be available to them (fundraising, *****, etc).                IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1  Family Background & Social Support -  1  Financial/Insurance  - 2  Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1  Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1  Adherence - 1  Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2  Health Literacy -  1  Coping Skills - 2     Total:  12 Low/Moderate Risk     The family scores as low/ moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.     The primary concerns are the financial stressors secondary to displacement, ******'s anxiety, and the patient and family's emotional readiness for transplant.         Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.    *Assist family with financial resources   *Assist pt with positive coping strategies by engaging Child ****, psych, and other supportive services        ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****[SM1]adherence
